name: Northwest Territories
summary: Blue, white and blue vertical bands, the white as wide as the flag is tall, with the territorial shield in the centre.
origin: Robert Bessant won a national competition, and the flag was adopted on 1 January 1969, after the territorial capital moved to Yellowknife.

symbols.name: Shield
symbols.description: A white chief with a wavy blue line, and below, green and red divided diagonally by a wavy line, with gold billets and a fox's head.
symbols.meaning: The polar ice cap and the Northwest Passage; the tree line between forest (green) and tundra (red); minerals (gold billets) and the fur trade (white fox).

facts: The central white pale uses the same proportions as Canada's national flag.
Nunavut was split off from the Northwest Territories in 1999.
The wavy line on the shield represents the Northwest Passage.
clues: Blue and white vertical bands with a shield showing a fox's head and a wavy line.
Its shield marks the tree line between forest and tundra.
A new territory was carved from it in 1999.
